brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
Tomiya-cha is a revived Japanese tea from around the old Tomiya post town in Miyagi Prefecture, grown from surviving local plants.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is said to go back to Date Masamune, who had seedlings brought from Kyoto. Travelers on the Oshu road drank it, an old road song mentions it, and it was presented to the lords of Sendai and shipped to Kyoto. A single early-summer picking could not compete once cheaper tea arrived in the Meiji era, and growing had ended by 1970. A local project started in 2017, with a first picking in 2018. In 2020 there were 3,000 plants on 3,000 square meters, and in 2023 it entered the Slow Food Ark of Taste.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: One picking a year, in early summer, because of the cold northern climate.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Expect what green teas usually give: fresh, vegetal and lightly sweet.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
